title: PM celebrates World Rhino Day
text:
PM shares initiation of Project Rhino
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today celebrated the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros on the occasion of World Rhino Day and lauded all those at the forefront of its protection. He noted that Assam now holds nearly 80 percent of the world’s rhino population and that Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.
The Prime Minister highlighted that rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal, while the successful reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, is creating history. He stated that this demonstrates the sustained commitment of the people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states. Furthermore, to take species conservation forward in the country, he shared that Project Rhino has been initiated to provide financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement, and understanding population dynamics.
In a post on X, the Prime Minister wrote:
“On World Rhino Day, we celebrate the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros and laud all those at the forefront of its protection.
Assam now holds nearly 80% of the world’s rhino population and Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.On one hand, rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal. On the other hand, success of reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa (Uttar Pradesh) is creating history. This shows the sustained commitment of our people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states.
Taking species conservation in the country forward, I am happy to share that Project Rhino has been initiated for financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement and understanding population dynamics.”

title: PM distributes more than 51,000 appointment letters to the newly appointed youth in Government at 20th Rozgar Mela
text:
India’s Yuva Shakti is at the heart of our journey towards a Viksit Bharat.: PM
The Rozgar Mela reflects our commitment to creating new opportunities for the youth: PM
Our youth’s talent and skills have earned global confidence; the world pins great hopes on our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our vibrant youth force: PM
Free Trade Agreements are unlocking new avenues of opportunity for our youth; these trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for our entrepreneurs, while creating fresh career possibilities for our youth: PM
India is currently the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem; Moreover, India’s startup story is no longer confined to major metropolitan areas, today, roughly half of all recognized startups are based in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities: PM
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various government organizations at the 20th Rozgar Mela today via video conferencing. Addressing on the occasion, he emphasized that this milestone brings immense joy to thousands of families, serving as a tribute to both the personal hard work of the candidates and the immense sacrifices made by their parents. “I wish you all the very best for this new beginning in life,” remarked Shri Modi.
Welcoming the new appointees into the Government of India as the nation marches toward the monumental milestone of a developed nation by 2047, the Prime Minister emphasized the pivotal role of youth in continuously empowering the twin campaigns of a developed and self-reliant India through every administrative decision. He highlighted their special responsibility toward fellow youth, noting that the talent and skills of the younger generation have captured the world’s trust, fueling immense global expectations from Indian innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power.”The world has high hopes from our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our youth power,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the recently concluded BRICS Summit, the Prime Minister stated that the administration’s strategy is to expand international cooperation far beyond traditional government-to-government interactions. He explained that initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal are designed to integrate entrepreneurs, farmers, women, and the youth directly into global partnerships. “Everyone should become an active participant in this partnership,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the economic diplomacy of the past few years, the Prime Minister pointed out that Free Trade Agreements with approximately 40 countries are unlocking unprecedented career possibilities. He emphasized that these agreements forge new markets and dynamic partnerships for domestic entrepreneurs while expanding career horizons for the youth. “These Free Trade Agreements are creating new doors of possibilities for our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the government’s sustained focus on future-ready skilling, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the National Education Policy, the Skill India Mission, the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships. He highlighted the PM-SETU scheme, which is modernizing one thousand government ITIs with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees alongside direct industry participation. “Our endeavor is that the education and skills of the youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy,” asserted Shri Modi.
Praising the explosive growth of the domestic startup ecosystem, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation’s position as the world’s third-largest startup hub, noting that nearly half of recognized startups now hail from tier-two and tier-three cities. He commended the youth from smaller towns for actively working on their ideas, building companies, and generating new employment opportunities for their peers. “Today the youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a major role in India’s new economy,” observed Shri Modi.
Outlining the strategy to boost private sector employment, the Prime Minister highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana, a massive one lakh crore rupee initiative aiming to introduce two crore youths into the formal workforce for the first time. He detailed that the scheme offers up to 15,000 rupees in incentives for first-time employees while also financially rewarding employers who generate new jobs. “The government is working on every front to increase employment in the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Connecting job creation to robust macroeconomic health, the Prime Minister explained that new youth opportunities emerge only when the economy grows, investments increase, and new industries expand. He highlighted the nation’s impressive 7.8 percent growth rate and a 12 percent surge in investments during the first quarter, noting that rating agencies are upgrading the nation’s economic outlook despite pervasive global uncertainties. “The reforms of the past years have a major contribution behind this growth of India,” noted Shri Modi.
Directing the new officials to embrace an era of continuous administrative transformation, the Prime Minister stressed the critical need to simplify tax compliance, enhance the ease of doing business, implement reforms in education and skilling, and open new sectors to innovation. He tasked the young bureaucrats with ensuring that the momentum of governance improvements remains unstoppable throughout their tenures. “It is necessary that the Reform Express in the country runs continuously at full speed,” asserted Shri Modi.
Invoking his poetic remarks about claiming the sun, the sea, the boat, and the sailor to conquer the waves, the Prime Minister challenged the new recruits to match this courage by championing the deep aspirations of the country’s youth. He insisted that every file signature and every administrative decision must actively clear hurdles, allow ideas to flourish, and promote innovation-driven investment that ultimately creates employment. “Your signature on every file should be one that advances youth aspirations,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Appealing to their personal journeys, the Prime Minister urged the fresh appointees to utilize their new authority within the government system with deep empathy. He advised them to actively dismantle the bureaucratic hurdles they themselves faced before joining the service. “Your effort should be that the difficulties you have gone through, other youths should not have to go through them,” remarked Shri Modi.
Encouraging a mindset of lifelong learning in a rapidly changing world, the Prime Minister directed the recruits to continuously upgrade their skills and master new technologies through the Mission Karmayogi framework. He noted that the ‘Karmayogi Prarambh’ module has been specifically designed to help new entrants navigate the system, joining the 1.7 crore employees already on the iGOT platform. “The more you improve yourself, the better you will be able to serve the citizens of the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that the true strength of any government lies in public trust, the Prime Minister reminded the recruits that their daily work, from processing elderly pensions to student scholarships and farmer subsidies, directly impacts common lives. He stressed that their behavior, efficiency, honesty, and sensitivity will ultimately define the citizen’s personal experience with the state. “Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty, all this will determine what that citizen’s experience with the government is like,” observed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with a powerful administrative mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the new officials to adopt the philosophy of ‘Nagrik Devo Bhava’ (The Citizen is Divine) in their daily service, equating citizen service to national service. He expressed his unwavering belief that they will fulfill their duties with utmost dedication and service across all departments. “Your success will be even greater when your work makes a citizen’s life easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: PM’s remarks during 20th Rozgar Mela via VC
text:
मेरे प्यारे युवा साथियों,
देश में त्योहारों का समय शुरू हो चुका है। इन खुशियों के बीच, आज का दिन हजारों परिवारों के जीवन में एक नई खुशी लेकर आया है। आज देश के 51 हजार से अधिक युवाओं को सरकारी सेवा के लिए नियुक्ति पत्र मिल रहे हैं। आज आप जिस मुकाम पर पहुंचे हैं, उसके पीछे आपकी मेहनत तो है ही, साथ ही,आपके माता-पिता और आपके परिवारजनों की भी तपस्या है। मैं आप सभी युवा साथियों को और आपके परिवारजनों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं। जीवन की इस नई शुरुआत के लिए आप सभी को शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।
साथियों,
आज आप सभी एक ऐसे समय में भारत सरकार से जुड़े हैं, जब देश एक बहुत बड़े लक्ष्य की ओर आगे बढ़ रहा है, और ये लक्ष्य है- 2047 तक विकसित भारत बनाने का। इसमें आप जैसे युवाओं की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका है। सरकार में रहते हुए आपको हर वो निर्णय लेना है, जो विकसित भारत के अभियान को, आत्मनिर्भर भारत के अभियान को निरंतर सशक्त करे। युवा होने के नाते विशेषतौर पर अन्य युवाओं के प्रति आपकी विशेष जिम्मेदारी है। आज आप देख रहे हैं, हमारे युवाओं के टैलेंट और स्किल्स ने पूरी दुनिया का भरोसा जीता है। दुनिया को हमारे innovators, हमारे entrepreneurs और हमारी युवा शक्ति से बहुत उम्मीदें है। अभी कुछ दिन पहले ही ब्रिक्स समिट संपन्न हुई। भारत का प्रयास रहा है कि BRICS cooperation केवल सरकारों तक सीमित न रहे, हमारे entrepreneurs, हमारे किसान, हमारी महिलाएं, हमारे युवा, हर कोई इस partnership का सक्रिय भागीदार बने। इसी सोच के साथ BRICS CONNECT और BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal की भी पहल की गई है।
साथियों,
भारत ने बीते कुछ वर्षों में करीब 40 देशों के साथ फ्री ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट भी किए हैं। ये फ्री ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट्स, FTA, हमारे युवाओं के लिए संभावनाओं के नए द्वार बना रहे हैं। इस तरह के ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट्स से हमारे entrepreneurs के लिए नई partnerships के रास्ते खुलते हैं, नए markets के रास्ते खुलते हैं। और हमारे युवाओं के लिए करियर में नई possibilities बनती हैं।
साथियों,
बीते वर्षों में भारत सरकार का निरंतर जोर युवाओं को भविष्य के लिए तैयार करने पर रहा है। National Education Policy, Skill India Mission, प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना या अप्रेंटिसशिप को बढ़ावा देने के प्रयास। हमारी कोशिश है कि युवाओं की पढ़ाई और उनकी skills, बदलती economy की जरूरतों के साथ चलें। जैसे एक उदाहरण है, PM-SETU। इस योजना के माध्यम से 60 हजार करोड़ रुपए के निवेश से एक हजार सरकारी ITIs को आधुनिक बनाया जा रहा है। इसमें इंडस्ट्री की सीधी भागीदारी सुनिश्चित की गई है।
साथियों,
भारत के युवाओं के सामर्थ्य की एक और तस्वीर हमारे startup ecosystem में दिखाई देती है। भारत आज दुनिया का तीसरा सबसे बड़ा startup ecosystem है। और भारत की startup story अब केवल बड़े शहरों की कहानी नहीं है। आज करीब आधे recognised startups टीयर-टू और टीयर-थ्री शहरों में हैं। यानी आज गांव, कस्बे और छोटे शहर का युवा भी भारत की नई economy में अपनी भूमिका बड़ी बना रहा है। छोटे शहरों के हमारे युवा अपने ideas पर काम कर रहे हैं, नई companies बना रहे हैं, और अपने साथ दूसरे युवाओं के लिए भी रोजगार के नए अवसर तैयार कर रहे हैं।
साथियों,
हमारा प्रयास है कि private sector में भी रोजगार के नए अवसर तेजी से बढ़ें। इसी सोच के साथ प्रधानमंत्री विकसित भारत रोजगार योजना शुरू की गई है। इस योजना पर करीब एक लाख करोड़ रुपए खर्च किए जा रहे हैं। इस योजना की मदद से करीब दो करोड़ युवाओं को पहली बार workforce का हिस्सा बनने का मौका मिलेगा। सरकार द्वारा इस योजना के तहत पहली बार नौकरी पाने वाले युवाओं को15 हजार रुपए तक का incentive भी दिया जा रहा है। नए रोजगार पैदा करने वाले employers को भी सरकार प्रोत्साहन दे रही है। यानि देश में रोजगार बढ़ाने के लिए सरकार हर मोर्चे पर काम कर रही है।
साथियों,
युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर तभी बनते हैं, जब देश की इकोनॉमी आगे बढ़ती है, जब investment बढ़ता है, नए उद्योग लगते हैं, और नए सेक्टर्स का विस्तार होता है। आज भारत तेजी से ग्रो करने वाली बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है। इस financial year की पहली तिमाही में भारत की growth rate 7.8 प्रतिशत रही है। Investment में करीब 12 प्रतिशत की बढ़ोतरी हुई है। रेटिंग एजेंसियां, भारत की रेटिंग्स सुधार रही हैं। और ये प्रगति ऐसे समय में हो रही है, जब दुनिया अनेक अनिश्चितताओं से गुजर रही है। भारत की इस growth के पीछे बीते वर्षों के reforms का बड़ा योगदान है। आपको अपने कार्यकाल में निरंतर reforms को और गति देनी है। Tax और compliance को सरल बनाना हो, ईज ऑफ डूइंग बिजनेस को बढ़ाना हो, एजुकेशन और स्किलिंग में reform हों, या नए सेक्टर्स को इनोवेशन के लिए खोलना हो या ईज ऑफ लिविंग की बात हो, हर स्तर पर देश में Reform Express का लगातार फुल स्पीड में चलना जरूरी है। और सरकारी कर्मचारी होने के नाते वर्तमान और आने वाले वर्षों में इसमें आप सभी की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका रहेगी।
साथियों,
मैंने कुछ दिन पहले कहा था, सूरज हमारा हो, समंदर भी हमारा हो। सूरज हमारा हो, समंदर भी हमारा हो। नाव हमारी हो, नाव हमारी हो, नाविक भी हमारा हो। लहरों पर विजय लिखें, लहरों पर विजय लिखें, वो हौसला हमारा हो। आज भारत का युवा इसी हौसले के साथ आगे बढ़ रहा है। अब आप सभी की भारत सरकार में रहते हुए ये जिम्मेदारी है कि देश के युवाओं की आकांक्षाओं को समझते हुए आप अपने काम को बखूबी निभाएं। मेरा फिर आग्रह होगा, आपका हर निर्णय, हर फाइल पर किया गया सिग्नेचर, युवा Aspirations को आगे बढ़ाने वाला होना चाहिए। आपको अपने कार्यकाल में देखना होगा, युवाओं के रास्ते की बाधाएं हटें, उनके ideas को आगे बढ़ाने का अवसर मिले, innovation से investment बढ़े और investment से employment के नए अवसर बनें।
साथियों,
अब आप स्वयं सरकारी व्यवस्था का हिस्सा बनने जा रहे हैं। इसलिए आपका प्रयास हो कि जिन परेशानियों से आप गुजरे हैं या जिन परेशानियों से आपके माता-पिता को गुजरना पड़ा है, उनसे दूसरे युवाओं को न गुजरना पड़े। जो तकलीफें आपके मां-बाप ने सही है, जो तकलीफें कभी आपको सहनी पड़ी हैं, वो अब हमारे देश के किसी नागरिक को सहनी ना पड़े, ये काम आपको सरकारी व्यवस्था में आते ही करना चाहिए।
साथियों,
आज देश में, हर क्षेत्र में तेजी से परिवर्तन हो रहा है। आप लगातार सीखते हुए, यहां तक पहुंचे हैं, अब यहां से निरंतर सीखते रहने की एक नई यात्रा शुरू हो रही है। आपको लगातार अपनी skills को बेहतर करना है। नई Technology और नए systems को समझना है। मिशन कर्मयोगी इसी उद्देश्य को पूरा करने में आपकी मदद करता है। iGOT Karmayogi Platform पर आज एक करोड़ 70 लाख से अधिक सरकारी कर्मचारी जुड़ चुके हैं। और आप जैसे नए साथियों के लिए कर्मयोगी प्रारंभ को विशेष रूप से तैयार किया गया है। आप जितना खुद को बेहतर बनाएंगे, उतना ही बेहतर देश के नागरिकों की सेवा कर पाएंगे।
साथियों,
आपको एक और बात हमेशा याद रखनी है। सरकार की असली ताकत देश के नागरिकों का विश्वास होता है। आप किसी भी मंत्रालय में हों, किसी भी विभाग में हों, आपका काम किसी न किसी रूप में देश के सामान्य नागरिक के जीवन को छुएगा। किसी बुजुर्ग की पेंशन आपके काम से आगे बढ़ेगी। किसी विद्यार्थी की स्कॉलरशिप आपकी जिम्मेदारी से जुड़ी होगी। किसी किसान को मिलने वाली सुविधा आपके डिपार्टमेंट में से हो जाती होगी। हो सकता है, किसी नागरिक के लिए आप ही सरकार का चेहरा हो। आपका व्यवहार, आपकी संवेदनशीलता, आपकी efficiency, आपकी ईमानदारी, इन सबसे तय होगा कि उस नागरिक का सरकार के साथ अनुभव कैसा रहता है।
इसलिए साथियों,
सरकारी सेवा में हमारा मंत्र होना चाहिए- नागरिक देवो भव, नागरिक देवो भव। नागरिक की सेवा, राष्ट्र की सेवा है। आपकी सफलता तब और बड़ी होगी, जब आपके काम से किसी नागरिक का जीवन आसान होगा। मुझे विश्वास है, आप जहां भी रहेंगे, जिस भी विभाग में रहेंगे, कर्तव्य और सेवा भाव से अपने दायित्व को निभाते रहेंगे। मैं एक बार फिर आप सभी को बधाई देता हूं।
बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

title: PM inaugurates International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
text:
India is showing how development and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand: PM
Often, the responsibility for carbon emissions has been unfairly placed on developing countries; However, the historical truth is that even today, India’s contribution to per capita carbon emissions is less than half of the global average: PM
Over the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field and sector related to the environment; Our major focus has been on renewable energy, which has played a significant role in environmental protection: PM
Among the G-20, India is the only country to have met the commitments made at the COP-21 Summit in Paris ahead of time: PM
Our development is both speedy and sustainable: PM
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” today at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation’s profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers. “India is now providing solutions to modern climate challenges,” asserted Shri Modi.
Addressing the flawed global narrative regarding carbon footprints, the Prime Minister pointed out that developing nations are unjustly blamed, despite developed nations emitting up to six times more carbon per capita than India. He detailed how the nation uses international platforms to assert this historical truth and showcase its traditional environmental strengths, recalling the launch of the “Convenient Action- Continuity for Change” book at COP-21 and the creation of platforms like One Sun, One World, One Grid, the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Global Biofuel Alliance, and the International Big Cat Alliance. “We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Bridging ancient philosophy with modern execution, the Prime Minister detailed the extraordinary progress made across every environmental sector over the past dozen years, specifically highlighting a massive strategic pivot toward renewable energy. He proudly stated that the nation proudly occupies a unique position within the G-20 for having achieved its COP-21 commitments ahead of schedule, setting global benchmarks in non-fossil fuels and solar capacity. “India’s performance on every parameter is a topic of discussion in the world today,” noted Shri Modi.
Presenting stark evidence of the nation’s solar revolution, the Prime Minister cited the leap from a mere 2 gigawatts of capacity a dozen years ago to over 160 gigawatts today, fueled by the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana which has solarized over 50 lakh homes with financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. He added that 30 lakh farmers have received solar pumps under the Kusum Yojana, while the completed One Nation-One Grid project has successfully prevented 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions. “We have started a mission to make homes themselves the center of solar power generation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Expanding on the massive strides in the broader clean energy landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted the threefold increase in wind capacity, significant hydro expansions, and a newly energized focus on nuclear power generation that now welcomes private players. He noted that these combined efforts have nearly quadrupled the nation’s non-fossil energy capacity while advancing cleaner technologies like Coal Gasification. “India has achieved major milestones in other sectors of clean energy as well,” noted Shri Modi.
Celebrating the dawn of advanced clean mobility, the Prime Minister proudly announced the recent launch of the country’s first Hydrogen Train, which also holds the record as the world’s longest. He described this technological leap as a foundational milestone for the future of green transportation. “This is the beginning of a new era of clean mobility,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the massive adoption of green vehicles, the Prime Minister highlighted a staggering 950-fold increase in Electric Vehicles, jumping from under three thousand sales before 2014 to roughly 25 lakh last year. He also pointed out that the modern FASTag system on highways and expressways has drastically reduced fuel wastage by minimizing wait times at toll booths. “India is embracing this opportunity of the EV revolution with full force,” noted Shri Modi.
Showcasing the sweeping modernization of public transport infrastructure, the Prime Minister contrasted the meager five-city, 250-kilometer metro network of 2014 with today’s expansive system operating in over 20 cities. “India has joined the ranks of those countries in the world that have a metro network of more than a thousand kilometers,” asserted Shri Modi.
Underscoring the eco-friendly transformation of heavy logistics, the Prime Minister explained how the near-total electrification of the railways has saved crores of liters of diesel from being burned. He highlighted the massive environmental benefits of the newly inaugurated 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, where historic double-stack container trains are replacing hundreds of polluting trucks per journey. “You can imagine on what a large scale this is helping the environment,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing to alternative eco-friendly transport modes, the Prime Minister celebrated the operationalization of approximately 5,000 kilometers of inland waterways across the country. He explained that a single standard inland vessel navigating these routes can carry a load equivalent to dozens of trucks. “This too is providing great help in environmental conservation,” noted Shri Modi.
Summarizing the collective impact of these transit upgrades, the Prime Minister emphasized that the sweeping changes across the entire mobility sector serve as undeniable proof of the nation’s balanced growth trajectory. He stated that rapid progress is entirely compatible with environmental preservation. “Our development is speedy as well as sustainable,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Praising the unprecedented mass participation in water conservation, the Prime Minister celebrated the construction of over 70,000 Amrit Sarovars and 1.5 crore rainwater harvesting structures under the Catch the Rain campaign. He noted that modern irrigation techniques under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and ‘Per Drop, More Crop’ are actively saving water for over 2 crore farmers. “Unprecedented work is being done on water conservation in India,” noted Shri Modi.
Championing the global revival of millets, the Prime Minister explained how promoting the cultivation of water-efficient Shree Anna has boosted domestic production and increased exports to 1.5 lakh tons, simultaneously creating economic opportunities and conserving water. He credited these relentless national efforts for inspiring the global celebration of 2023 as the International Year of Millets. “Because of this model, the world is also joining us,” remarked Shri Modi.’
Underscoring the massive scale of ecological agriculture, the Prime Minister detailed the establishment of 24,000 natural farming clusters across 12.5 lakh hectares under the National Mission on Natural Farming. He also highlighted the successful development of 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties and the strategic promotion of agro-forestry to reduce the national footprint. “By promoting agro-forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the comprehensive nature of the country’s environmental efforts, the Prime Minister shared that the very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent over the last 12 years. He praised the ongoing ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign for inspiring citizens to plant crores of trees in a continuous, nationwide drive.
Addressing the critical challenge of plastic pollution, the Prime Minister reiterated the national ban on single-use plastics and the strong push toward a Circular Economy based on reducing, reusing, and recycling thousands of tons of daily waste. He cited the Gobardhan Yojana as a prime example of converting rural organic waste into valuable resources through a Wealth from Waste model. “Our endeavor is that instead of treating waste as a problem, it should be transformed into a resource,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Elevating the significance of the nation’s environmental achievements, the Prime Minister stated that these robust statistics represent far more than domestic progress. He framed the nation’s developmental data as monumental, direct contributions to the survival and prosperity of the entire human race. “These are also figures of India’s contribution to the future of humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored the profound relationship between the earth and its inhabitants that drives these responsible actions. He concluded his address on an optimistic note, expressing deep confidence that the conference deliberations would yield innovative solutions, and offered his final felicitations. “India is also working to build a responsible and sustainable future,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: PM’s address at the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
text:
Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Bhupender Yadav ji, Attorney General of India R. Venkataramani ji, National Green Tribunal (NGT) Chairman Justice Prakash Srivastava ji, all distinguished dignitaries present in this hall, ladies and gentlemen.
For centuries, India has guided the world on the subject of nature and environment. With that ideological commitment, and based on our cultural experiences, India is now also providing solutions to modern climate challenges, while at the same time calling for collective efforts of humanity. I am happy that this NGT conference is carrying forward that mission. For this event, I extend my congratulations and best wishes to all the officials of NGT and all dignitaries associated with it.
Friends,
We all know that often the responsibility for carbon emissions has been wrongly placed on developing countries. Many of my companions from the Global South are present here. But the historical truth is that even today, India’s per capita carbon emissions are less than half the global average. In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s. Six times higher. India presents this fact strongly on global platforms. And I say to every Indian – show your strength too. We have also presented our traditions and their power before the world. On these very subjects, during COP‑21 in Paris, we launched the book Convenient Action – Continuity for Change. We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along. Whether it is the vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid, or the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, Global Biofuel Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance, Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) – each of these platforms is becoming a stage for India’s dedicated commitments on climate and environment.
Friends,
Today’s India is moving forward by weaving its ancient ideas of environmental protection into a modern vision. In the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every sector related to the environment. Our major focus has been on renewable energy, and this has played a big role in environmental protection. India is the only country in the G20 – I say this before the big leaders of the G20 – the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about. On every parameter – non‑fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions – India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide. Look at the figures. Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts. Twelve years ago – 2 gigawatts. If there are lawyers here, please note these figures, they may come in handy. Today it has crossed 160 gigawatts. From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years. Under the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, we launched the mission to make homes themselves centers of solar power generation. Under this scheme, more than 5 million homes have already installed rooftop solar panels. This is more than the total number of homes in many countries. For this, the government has provided financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. Under the KUSUM scheme, the government has installed solar pumps in the fields of 3 million farmers. We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project. Not only this – LED bulbs in homes have proven successful in saving electricity. Crores of LED bulbs have been distributed to households. And the results of these efforts are before us today. From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.
Friends,
Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors. In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled. Hydropower capacity has increased significantly. And now the country is working rapidly on nuclear energy generation. Those who give long speeches on the environment – when I advance nuclear energy work, they will stand in the courts to stop it. A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector. Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled. India is also promoting technologies like coal gasification for cleaner use of coal.
Friends,
India is now working rapidly in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen. Just a few days ago, India’s first hydrogen train was launched – and it is the world’s longest hydrogen train. This marks the beginning of a new era of clean mobility.
Friends,
In 12 years, the number of electric vehicles in our country has increased nearly 950 times. 950 times. In the year before 2014, fewer than 3,000 EVs were sold in India. Last year, nearly 2.5 million EVs were sold in India. That means India is embracing the opportunity of the EV revolution with full strength, and this is also helping the environment. On our highways and expressways, modern fast‑track systems have reduced waiting at toll booths. This has stopped the fuel wastage that used to occur at toll booths.
Friends,
Until 2014, in five cities of our country there was less than 250 kilometers of metro network. Lawyers here should note this figure. Before 2014, only five cities had less than 250 kilometers. Today, metros run in more than 20 cities, and India has joined the countries with more than 1,000 kilometers of metro network.
Friends,
With nearly 100 percent electrification of railways, billions of liters of diesel burning has been avoided. The environment has been protected. Just this month, a 3,000‑kilometer‑long Dedicated Freight Corridor was inaugurated. Every train running on it carries loads equal to hundreds of trucks from one place to another. The operation of double‑stack container freight trains is historic in itself. You can imagine how greatly this helps the environment.
Friends,
Today, transportation is happening on about 5,000 kilometers of waterways in the country. This is the most environment‑friendly mobility. A standard inland vessel running on these waterways carries loads equal to dozens of trucks in one journey. This too is greatly helping environmental protection.
Friends,
All these changes in the mobility sector alone are proof that our development is both speedy and sustainable.
Friends,
Today, with the participation of millions of people, unprecedented work is happening in India on water conservation. I am happy that more than 70,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed in the country. Under the Catch the Rain campaign, nearly 15 million water harvesting structures have been built, preserving rainwater. Through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, more than 20 million farmers today are connected with modern irrigation facilities. Initiatives like Per Drop More Crop are also saving water. Shri Anna – that is, millets – are another great successful example. India is promoting the cultivation of millets, which consume less water. In recent years, millet production has increased in the country, and exports have risen to about 150,000 tonnes. This is creating new opportunities for farmers, while also saving water. And because of this model, the world is joining us. Thanks to India’s efforts, 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.
Friends,
Under the National Mission on Natural Farming, today about 1.25 million hectares in the country have developed 24,000 clusters of natural farming. Not only this, nearly 3,000 varieties of climate‑resilient crops have also been developed in the country. By promoting agro‑forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints.
Friends,
How wide‑ranging our efforts are can be seen in India’s forest coverage. This too I mention for my lawyer friends. In the past 12 years, our very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent. This is a very big achievement. Under the campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (One Tree in the Name of Mother), crores of trees have been planted across the country. And this campaign continues.
Friends,
Plastic waste has also been a major challenge for the environment. That is why India has banned single‑use plastic. With the mantra of reduce, reuse, and recycle, we have promoted the circular economy. Today, thousands of tonnes of waste are being recycled every day in India. Through the Gobardhan Yojana, cow dung and other organic waste in villages are being converted into useful resources. Our effort is that waste should not be seen as a problem, but transformed into a resource under the Waste to Wealth model.
Friends,
All these figures are not just India’s development statistics – they are India’s contributions for the future of humanity.
Friends,
Our cultural thought is – “Mata bhumih, putro aham prithivyah” – meaning, this earth is our mother and we are her children. title: PM to inaugurate International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September
text:
Conference to facilitate dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance
Conference to witness participation of eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries and distinguished participants from India
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September 2026 at around 10 AM at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
The two-day Conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal on 19 and 20 September 2026. It will witness the participation of environmental experts, Judges of the Supreme Court of India and High Courts, District Court Judges, Secretaries of various Ministries, senior government officials, representatives of State Judicial Academies, State Legal Services Authorities, State Expert Appraisal Committees (SEACs), State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAAs), State Wetland Authorities and other stakeholders. It will also bring together eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries.
The Conference will provide a platform for the exchange of judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences across jurisdictions. It will facilitate dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement, and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.

title: PM addresses a gathering during the release of instalment under the Annapurna Yojana in West Bengal
text:
Annapurna Yojana is a big boost for Nari Shakti in West Bengal: PM
It is the goal of our government that not a single eligible woman should be deprived of the benefits of the Annapurna Yojana: PM
With the strength of a Viksit Bengal, the resolution of a Viksit Bharat will become even stronger: PM
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today, addressed a gathering during the release of instalment under the Annapurna Yojana in West Bengal via video conferencing. Expressing his profound joy at connecting with the citizens on a special occasion, the Prime Minister conveyed his deepest respects to the mothers and sisters of Bengal. He emphasized that their unwavering trust and affinity serve as a massive source of personal empowerment. “Your trust is my strength!” remarked Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the cultural significance of the day, the Prime Minister took a moment to celebrate a sacred festival dedicated to creation and craftsmanship. He extended his warmest greetings to all the citizens honoring this special occasion. “I extend my heartiest greetings to all of you on Vishwakarma Puja,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the dawn of a transformative era in the state, the Prime Minister celebrated the introduction of a new tradition designed to empower local women through the Annapurna Yojana. He extended his heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to every female beneficiary stepping into this new chapter of capability. “Today, new capabilities have been added to the mothers and sisters of Bengal,” noted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the immense domestic responsibilities shouldered by women, the Prime Minister acknowledged how they meticulously manage families through countless daily decisions. He pointed out that alleviating their financial anxieties regarding essential expenses naturally elevates their self-assurance. “When they have less worry about necessary expenses, their self-confidence increases even more,” observed Shri Modi.
Describing the Annapurna Yojana as a crucial intervention to bolster female confidence, the Prime Minister detailed how a guaranteed monthly deposit provides profound life support. He noted that receiving this fixed amount without having to ask anyone ensures financial dignity for the women. “This is a huge support for their lives. This is a big help!” asserted Shri Modi.
Presenting the tangible impact of the initiative, the Prime Minister announced that the fourth installment of 3,000 rupees is successfully reaching the bank accounts of approximately 1.5 crore sisters. He explained that this recurring financial assistance serves as a vital lifeline for purchasing medicines, household necessities, or funding a child’s education. “For a sister, it could be a support to buy medicine or essential household items,” noted Shri Modi
Outlining the broader vision behind the financial assistance, the Prime Minister stated his firm belief in endowing women with robust decision-making power and the courage to advance. He congratulated the beneficiaries while reaffirming the central role the Annapurna scheme plays in this empowerment strategy. “The women of Bengal should also have the power of decision-making and the courage to move forward,” asserted Shri Modi.’
The Prime Minister credited the mothers and sisters of the state for playing the most pivotal role in ushering in political change after enduring numerous hardships. He emphasized that the new government’s primary benchmark is to improve their Ease of Living by adhering strictly to the mantra of ‘Less talk, more work’. “The very first test before our new government was to make the lives of Bengal’s women easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the rapid execution of the welfare agenda, the Prime Minister highlighted that work on the Annapurna Yojana commenced within days of the new government taking office. He celebrated the seamless, direct bank transfers reaching millions of women while strictly eliminating corrupt practices.Underscoring the administration’s commitment to absolute inclusivity, the Prime Minister assured that rapid efforts are underway to guarantee comprehensive coverage across the state. “It is also the goal of our government that not a single eligible woman should be deprived of the benefits of the Annapurna Yojana,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing a comprehensive lifecycle approach to female empowerment, the Prime Minister listed a multitude of prioritized interventions ranging from the Matru Vandana Yojana for pregnant women to the Beti Bachao – Beti Padhao movement. He enumerated sweeping initiatives, including building crores of school toilets, opening Sainik Schools for girls, providing Mudra loans, increasing maternity leave, delivering Ujjwala gas and Har Ghar Jal water connections, distributing Ayushman cards, and securing joint property rights under PM Awas, to comprehensively address every challenge faced by women from childhood through motherhood. “Solving every problem related to the life cycle of mothers, sisters, and daughters has been the highest priority,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister assured the public that the current administration is rapidly accelerating these previously stalled programs to ensure timely delivery. “Now, under the present government, these stalled schemes have been taken forward at a rapid pace,” noted Shri Modi.
Citing the PM Awas Yojana as a prime example of renewed momentum, the Prime Minister announced that over 50 lakh newly identified poor families in the state will soon receive permanent houses, alongside the rollout of the PM Vishwakarma Yojana. He attributed this revival of pending projects to the overwhelming blessings and support of the local women, projecting a collaborative vision for the state’s future. “We will all together build a new Bengal,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Linking regional progress to the national vision, the Prime Minister expressed absolute confidence that local women will continue to accelerate the development journey toward a Viksit Bharat. He emphasized that the nation’s overarching resolution is fundamentally strengthened by the capabilities of a developed state. “With the strength of a Viksit Bengal, the resolution of a Viksit Bharat will become even stronger,” asserted Shri Modi.’
Concluding his address with deep gratitude, the Prime Minister acknowledged that the continuous affection and blessings of the people serve as an endless inspiration for public service. He offered his final felicitations for the dual celebrations of the day. “Once again, many congratulations to you all on Annapurna Diwas,” remarked Shri Modi.’

title: PM’s remarks during the release of instalment under the Annapurna Yojana in West Bengal via VC
text:
Namaskar.
My respectful greetings and regards to all mothers of Bengal!
On this special occasion, I feel immense happiness to be connected with you. I have always received great affection from the mothers and sisters of Bengal. Your trust and warmth are a great source of strength for me.
Today is also the sacred occasion of Vishwakarma Puja. I extend my heartfelt wishes to all of you on Vishwakarma Puja.
Friends,
At this auspicious time, a new tradition is being strengthened in Bengal. Today, through the Annapurna Yojana, new empowerment is being connected with the mothers and sisters of Bengal. I congratulate and send my best wishes to every sister who is benefitting from this scheme.
Friends,
In our homes, mothers and sisters carry many responsibilities. Amidst numerous small and big decisions, a woman takes care of the family in every way. And when she has less worry about essential expenses, her confidence increases even more. The Annapurna Yojana is such an important effort to strengthen the confidence of Bengal’s women. Every month, a fixed amount reaches the bank accounts of Bengal’s sisters – an amount for which they do not have to ask anyone. This is a great support in their lives.
Friends,
Today, the fourth installment of the Annapurna Yojana is reaching the accounts of nearly 15 million sisters. That means 3,000 rupees every month. For a mother, this could be the expense of her child’s education. For a sister, it could be support for medicine or essential household items.
Friends,
Our vision is that Bengal’s women should have the power to make decisions and the courage to move forward. Annapurna Yojana plays a big role in this. I extend heartfelt congratulations to all mothers and sisters who are beneficiaries of the Annapurna Yojana.
Friends,
On May 4th this year, Bengal chose a new path of transformation. And I know, in this transformation, the most important role has been played by the mothers and sisters of Bengal. You have seen many hardships in your lives. You have waited for many things. Therefore, the first test before our new government was to make the lives of Bengal’s women easier, to increase ease of living in their lives. That is why the guiding mantra we adopted was – Less talk, more work.
Friends,
The Annapurna Yojana began with this very thought. Within just a few days of forming the government, work started on this scheme. And today, money is directly reaching the bank accounts of such a large number of women. No cut money, no middlemen!
Our government’s goal is that not a single eligible woman should be deprived of the benefits of the Annapurna Yojana. Work is progressing rapidly for this too.
Friends,
Solving every problem connected with the life cycle of mothers, sisters, and daughters has been the highest priority of the BJP. To ensure nutritious food for the child during pregnancy, we launched the Matru Vandana Yojana, sending money directly to women’s bank accounts. To prevent daughters from being eliminated in the womb, we started mass movements like Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao. To ensure daughters do not drop out of school due to lack of toilets, we built millions of toilets. To continue their education, we offered high interest in the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. To allow daughters to enter Sainik Schools, we opened their doors. To help daughters start their own work, we launched the Mudra Yojana with collateral‑free loans. To ensure mothers could continue their jobs after childbirth, we increased maternity leave. To provide new earning opportunities in villages, we gave record support to self‑help groups. To free daughters from smoke in the kitchen, we gave Ujjwala gas connections. To free them from the struggle of fetching water, we launched the Har Ghar Nal Se Jal scheme. To free them from darkness, we gave free electricity connections under the Saubhagya scheme. To ensure daughters do not hide their illness due to lack of money, we gave them the strength of the Ayushman card. title: PM’s speech during the inauguration of SEMICON India 2026
text:
Thank you very much.
Union Cabinet colleagues Ashwini Vaishnaw ji, Jitin Prasada ji, all industry leaders, CEOs, delegates, and virtually connected hundreds of universities and institutes – the future of India, my young companions. And here present, the large number of enthusiastic youth, ladies and gentlemen!
This is the fifth edition of Semicon India. I welcome you all. I extend a special welcome to the guests who have come from abroad.
Friends,
Today is also Vishwakarma Jayanti. I extend my best wishes to all countrymen on Vishwakarma Jayanti. In our tradition, Lord Vishwakarma is considered the symbol of the power of construction and creation. And see the coincidence – Semicon India begins today itself. On one side, our centuries‑old tradition of creation, and on the other side, the technology and vision of the 21st century – this is our inspiration for self‑reliant India, for developed India.
Friends,
Every citizen is committed to building a developed India. If we look at just the past 15 days – I draw your attention only to 15 days – we can see the direction and speed with which India is moving forward. In this September, just 10 days ago, the Global Fintech Fest was held in Mumbai. There was discussion on inclusive finance through agentic AI, tokenization, and quantum technologies. During the same period, nearly 3,000 kilometers of Dedicated Freight Corridor became fully operational in India. I am talking about September’s 10 days, not long ago. This will speed up freight movement in the country, improve logistics, and give new strength to manufacturing.
Friends,
In this same period, in this September itself, India’s quarterly GDP report came. And even in this challenging period, India achieved 7.8 percent growth. And during the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency upgraded India’s sovereign rating. And this happened after three decades – nearly 35 years. That means, on one side India’s economy is growing, and on the other side, the world’s trust in India is also increasing.
Friends,
Another big picture of this trust was seen just three days ago at the BRICS Summit. India successfully hosted this summit. The unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration is another big proof of the world’s trust in India.
Friends,
Amidst these achievements of India, this Semicon India event has become even more important. Its first edition was in 2022. Since then we meet every year, but every year the subject of our discussion has changed. In the first edition, we talked about policy. In the next editions, the discussion moved forward. We began talking about projects – from signing files to laying foundation stones. Last year we began discussing pilot lines and test chips. How the first samples began to come out of India’s units – this was discussed. And this year, we are talking about commercial production. Now chips are coming out of India’s plants and reaching customers in India and the world. And just now, in Mohali and Surat, commercial production has started in two more plants. I congratulate them as well.
Friends,
For any country, reaching here in such a short time is not easy. This is not a sector where you set up a factory and the work is done. It takes decades to build technological capabilities. Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, they have been prepared after decades of effort. But India, with your cooperation, has worked simultaneously on chip design, manufacturing, equipment manufacturing, materials ecosystem, testing capability – and has shown success. In this journey, you industry leaders have been the major stakeholders. You are the pillars of India’s success, you are the partners in our journey.
Friends,
In the semiconductor industry, there is a word – “tape‑out.” This is the day when a chip, after design completion, goes into production. But work does not stop after tape‑out. On that very day, work begins on the next version. And India is doing the same. India has started the second phase of the Semiconductor Mission. The size of our first phase was about 8 billion dollars, while the second phase we have set at 13.5 billion dollars. Moving on the Reform Express, we have made further reforms in this sector. Now international companies can also collaborate with our startups, Indian design companies, and OCI‑owned companies. That means whether it is policies, funds, regulatory frameworks – whatever is needed for the success of your projects, the Government of India is taking every step.
Friends,
Our effort is that fabless companies grow in India, and intellectual property creation also happens in India. Whether it is making different types of compound semiconductors, making silicon photonics part of the ecosystem, or enabling infrastructure for AI – all this is necessary. And in this direction, we must move forward together. The foundation needed for this has already been prepared. India is also focusing greatly on strengthening supply chains. Many reforms have been made for this. To the leaders of equipment companies present here, I say – do not lag behind in taking advantage of this. For leaders in chemicals, gases, and materials too, golden opportunities await in India. We want the entire ecosystem to grow together. For this, the demand pipeline is also ready. So far, 12 projects have been approved, and in the next phase this scope will expand further.
Friends,
Another advantage for all of you in India is youth – talented, skilled manpower. Today we have a very large pool of engineering talent. India has thousands of engineering colleges, and every year India produces lakhs of engineers. Once, a gentleman from an American company came to meet me. He said, “If we want to recruit engineers in our country, we call them, and they all fit in one room. But in India, if we call engineers, even a football field is too small.” This is India’s strength.
And Friends,
For chip designing, large‑scale skilling work is underway. Just before coming here, I met some young companions from industry on this very campus – all students. These students gifted me chips they had designed themselves. Our government has set a target to train one lakh engineering students for the semiconductor industry. And as you were told, we have already trained more than 70,000 youth. Such a large talent pool is nothing less than a gold mine for all of you.
Friends,
Amidst these government efforts, today I also appeal to the youth – young talents who are doing research in India should come forward. Those youth who are doing research abroad should also connect with the development of advanced technologies in India. I urge industry leaders to lead R&D in the country. This benefits industry, and it also strengthens India’s youth power.
Friends,
The advancing semiconductor industry also faces some challenges, which you are all familiar with. For years, people in your industry talked about transistor size. As transistors became smaller, computing became faster and more efficient. Even today this question is important. But now, with the arrival of Artificial Intelligence, some new questions have arisen before this industry. In the past two years, the global semiconductor market has grown by more than 20 percent. And a very big part of this growth is due to demand created by AI. That means, today if you are working on AI, the challenges are not only about what is inside the chip, but also about what is happening around it. Bringing memory closer to the processor, connecting many chips in such a way that they work together as one system, transferring huge amounts of data from here to there without delay, managing heat and power – these are many challenges before the semiconductor industry. Amidst these challenges, the world most needs new and reliable manufacturing locations. And India – I assure you – India is continuously preparing itself for this.
Friends,
Another major issue before today’s semiconductor industry is energy security. The chips being made for AI are used in AI data centers. In these data centers, thousands of high‑performance processors work together, processing huge amounts of data. As AI expands, the need for computing power will increase at the same pace. And as computing power increases, the need for electricity will also increase greatly. Therefore, investment in the power sector is very important. Where our plants are located, electricity must be available on time, in the required quantity when needed – this is very important. That is why India is making very large investments in the power sector today. In the past decade, our installed solar energy capacity has increased from about 2 gigawatts to more than 160 gigawatts – from 2 to 160. In nuclear energy too, we are moving forward rapidly. This sector has been opened to private players. We are also working on small modular reactors. In the past decade, India has also expanded its transmission network.
Friends,
This expansion of power infrastructure in India is also a great strength for our semiconductor ecosystem. India is taking every step needed to make itself a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry.
Friends,
India is the Mother of Democracy. Just a few years ago, our Constitution completed 75 years. When such a country succeeds in a critical industry, it strengthens the entire world’s supply chain. And today, when supply chains are being weaponized, its importance increases even more. We must see the developments happening in India from this larger perspective. India’s aspirations are before you, and the new opportunities being created in India are ready to welcome you. Once again, I extend many congratulations to all of you for this event.
Thank you very much.

title: PM inaugurates SEMICON India 2026
text:
India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly; It is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth: PM
India’s economy is growing; the world’s trust in India is also growing: PM

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion and highlighting the significance of the event’s fifth edition, the Prime Minister extended warm greetings to all participants. He expressed particular gratitude to the international attendees who had traveled to India to partake in the summit. “I extend a special welcome to the guests who have come to India from abroad,” remarked Shri Modi.
Drawing a powerful parallel between the launch of Semicon India and Vishwakarma Diwas, the Prime Minister honored the nation’s centuries-old heritage of construction and creation. He pointed out the beautiful coincidence of merging traditional creative power with 21st-century technology and vision. “This is our inspiration for a self-reliant India, a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.
Emphasizing the nation’s rapid progress over the past 15 days, the Prime Minister listed major milestones, including discussions on inclusive finance at the Global Fintech Fest, the operationalization of a 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, and a robust 7.8 percent quarterly GDP growth. He also highlighted the recent sovereign rating upgrade by a Japanese Credit Rating Agency as a testament to the nation’s soaring economic credibility. “Meaning, on one hand, India’s economy is growing, and on the other hand, the world’s trust in India is also increasing,” observed Shri Modi.
Recalling the diplomatic triumph of the recently concluded BRICS Summit hosted by India, the Prime Minister pointed to the unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration as a reflection of international consensus. He underscored that this historic diplomatic achievement validates the global community’s unwavering faith in the nation. “This is another major proof of the world’s trust in India,” noted Shri Modi.
Tracing the evolutionary journey of Semicon India since its inception in 2022, the Prime Minister mapped the progression from initial policy discussions to project planning, pilot lines, and finally, the commencement of commercial production. He celebrated the realization of these efforts with chips now reaching global customers, alongside the launch of commercial production in two new plants in Mohali and Surat. “Now our chips, coming out of India’s plants, have started reaching customers in the country and the world,” noted Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the immense complexity of building a semiconductor ecosystem, the Prime Minister praised the collaborative effort required to master chip design, equipment manufacturing, and testing capabilities in record time. He credited the present industry leaders as foundational pillars whose partnership made this rapid technological leap possible. “You are the pillars of this success of India, you are partners,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Outlining the relentless momentum of the sector, the Prime Minister explained the concept of ‘tape out’ and how the government continuously pushes for the next technological version without pause. He announced the massive 13.5 billion dollar second phase of the Semiconductor Mission and highlighted new regulatory reforms that facilitate collaborations between international companies, startups, and design firms. “The Government of India is taking every step needed for the success of your projects,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the vision for a robust domestic supply chain, the Prime Minister stressed the importance of nurturing fabless companies, creating intellectual property, and integrating silicon photonics for AI-enabling infrastructure. He urged leaders in equipment, chemicals, gases, and materials to capitalize on the golden opportunities presented by the twelve approved projects and an expanding demand pipeline. “We want the entire ecosystem to grow together,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the strategic advantage of India’s demographic dividend, the Prime Minister spoke of the vast pool of engineering talent and the extensive skilling initiatives specifically tailored for chip designing. He proudly mentioned receiving custom-designed chips from students and reiterated the government’s ambitious target to train one lakh engineering students, with 70,000 already trained. “Such a large talent pool is, in a way, nothing less than a gold mine for all of you,” remarked Shri Modi.
Calling upon the brilliant minds engaged in domestic and international research, the Prime Minister urged young talents to actively participate in developing advanced technologies within the country. He challenged industry leaders to spearhead local research and development, ensuring mutual growth for both businesses and the nation’s youth. “There is benefit for the industry in this, and the youth power of India will also get strength from this,” asserted Shri Modi.
Addressing the evolving complexities of the semiconductor market, the Prime Minister discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management. He positioned the nation as a reliable and continuously prepared destination to meet these new global manufacturing challenges. “India is constantly preparing itself for this,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Tackling the critical issue of energy security for high-performance computing, the Prime Minister outlined the massive power requirements generated by AI data centers and the necessity of uninterrupted electricity for manufacturing plants. He detailed the nation’s aggressive expansion in the power sector, including a leap to over 160 GW in solar capacity, the opening of nuclear energy to private players, and the development of small modular reactors. “Therefore, India today is making huge investments in the power sector as well,” noted Shri Modi.
Connecting the rapid expansion of power infrastructure to industrial readiness, the Prime Minister declared that this energy security acts as a fundamental strength for the semiconductor ecosystem. He reassured stakeholders that the administration is deeply committed to optimizing conditions for industrial growth. “India is taking every step that makes us a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by contextualizing the nation’s technological strides within its democratic ethos, the Prime Minister reminded the audience of the 75-year legacy of the Indian Constitution. He expressed that a successful critical industry in the ‘Mother of Democracy’ intrinsically fortifies the entire global supply chain, extending a warm invitation to explore the boundless opportunities ahead. “India’s aspirations are before you, and the new opportunities being created in India are ready to welcome you,” affirmed Shri Modi.’

title: Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
text:
Over 51 lakh additional employees expected to come under mandatory EPFO coverage
Decision strengthens formalisation and advances India’s long-term social security vision
Major step towards stronger retirement security and Viksit Bharat@2047
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers.
The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to Rs.15,000 in September 2014. The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years.
At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above Rs.15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. Raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 will bring a substantial segment of employees in the Rs.15,000– Rs.25,000 wage band within the statutory social security framework.
The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), in accordance with the applicable scheme provisions. It will also enable the statutory contribution and pensionable-wage framework to better reflect prevailing wage levels.
Since the wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, India has witnessed sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment. In several States and occupations, minimum wages have also moved closer to the existing threshold. The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.
The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.
The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about
Rs.11,339 crore
, against the existing annual budgetary support of about
Rs.10,250 crore
. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately
Rs.56,696 crore
.
EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.
India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.
This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.

title: PM to inaugurate SEMICON India 2026 on 17 September in New Delhi
text:

More than 600 companies and representatives from 52 countries to participate

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate SEMICON India 2026 on 17 September 2026 at around 10 AM at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi. Prime Minister will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The three-day conference and exhibition, being held from 17 to 19 September 2026, will be organised on the theme ‘Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem’. It will bring together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain. The conference will focus on advancing collaboration, investment, innovation and talent development in India. Parallel sessions will cover advancements in the display industry, six Country Roundtables designed to facilitate collaboration and joint ventures, a forum on women’s leadership, among other sessions.
SEMICON India 2026 will adopt a comprehensive value-chain approach, showcasing the journey from semiconductor materials, equipment and chip design to fabrication, advanced packaging, electronics and systems. The new ‘Sand to Silicon to Systems’ Value Chain Experience will present this journey across the semiconductor ecosystem.
SEMICON India 2026 will feature more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers. The exhibition will feature six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion.

title: PM’s opening address during the 18th BRICS Summit session: “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Development”
text:
Your Highness,
Excellencies,
Namaskar!
I extend a warm welcome to all of you to the extended family of BRICS.
Today, this hall brings together continents, cultures, and diverse development journeys. It is a testament to the growing strength, appeal, and unprecedented trust in BRICS.
Friends,
Under India’s Presidency, we have focused all our efforts on these four pillars: Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability. I am pleased that, with all your cooperation and support, we have been able to translate our shared vision into win-win cooperation.
Today, the number of conflicts and tensions in the world is continuously increasing, and this is having an increasingly negative and far-reaching impact on the lives of ordinary people.
Pandemics, climate disasters, and supply-chain disruptions have shown that in today’s interconnected world, no crisis remains confined to a single region. Therefore, within the BRICS group, we have placed special emphasis on strengthening Resilience. It is equally important to identify challenges in time, be prepared for them, and take prompt action.
With this approach, we have agreed on a BRICS Integrated Early Warning System for the prevention of and response to infectious diseases. Early Warning Data Integration Guidelines have been prepared for disaster management. The BRICS Logistics Supply Chain Cooperation Framework will help make our supply chains more reliable and resilient.
Friends,
Under Innovation, the BRICS Incubator Network will connect our start-ups and incubators with one another. To promote innovative and scalable solutions, we have proposed the BRICS Startup Innovation Fund.
The BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture will create new opportunities for farmers. Through this initiative, AI, geospatial technology, and Digital Public Infrastructure will be connected to the real needs of farmers.
The weaponization of technology and critical minerals can hinder our shared progress. Therefore, we have emphasised inclusivity in the adoption of technology.
Friends,
India has advanced friendship, partnership, and cooperation through the BRICS platform.
Our endeavour has been to ensure that BRICS cooperation does not remain limited to governments alone. We have sought to make our entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth, and ordinary citizens active participants in it.
Through BRICS CONNECT, we have promoted skills, employability, women in the workforce, social security, and capacity building.
To connect small enterprises with knowledge, finance, and new markets, we have initiated the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal.
The BRICS Urban Mobility Hub has been established to facilitate the sharing of best practices among our cities.
Friends,
In Indian civilisation, nature has been accorded the status of a mother. For centuries, we have believed that development and the environment are not alternatives to each other, but are complementary. Within BRICS as well, we have emphasised the need to strike a balance between human development and the environment.
This is the foundation of Sustainability. It is also our responsibility towards future generations. In this direction, we have made progress on several fronts.
For Smart Grids and Energy Storage, we have established the BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence. This will help make our clean energy systems more reliable, efficient, and accessible.
The Centres of Excellence for Agro-Ecology and Regenerative Agriculture will connect traditional knowledge with modern science. The principles developed for community-based climate adaptation will make indigenous knowledge an important foundation for climate action.
Friends,
Building on these four pillars, through BRICS we have sought to promote inclusive global growth. We believe that the benefits of solutions developed within BRICS should not remain confined to BRICS alone. They should be made adaptable and accessible to meet the needs of the Global South.
Friends,
From my personal experience, I can say that the Global South countries’ confidence in BRICS has grown, because within BRICS:
Their voices are heard.
Their experiences are respected.
And solutions are developed not for them, but together with them.
The strength of BRICS lies in our diversity and cooperation.
We may be rooted in different realities, but together, we rise through cooperation, and blossom for humanity.
May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation become our inspiration, and our progress serve the cause of all humanity.
Thank you very much.

title: PM chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” (September 12, 2026)
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” on September 12, 2026 during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
In his remarks, Prime Minister emphasized that:
• Global South is at the front row of global crises, but the back row of decision-making. We must turn the “pyramid of privilege” into a “platform of partnership”.
• Global governance must reflect today’s realities, with greater representation especially in institutions such as the UN Security Council.
• Efforts must be made to make the Global South move from being a rule-taker to a rule-shaper. Through BRICS, we can provide young diplomats and policymakers from the Global South with negotiation skills, practical training and legal expertise.
• Seafarers make a significant contribution to global trade, yet they often lack adequate support during times of crisis and proposed establishing a Seafarers Emergency Support Network.

title: BRICS New Delhi Declaration: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability (September 12, 2026)
text:
1. We, the Leaders of BRICS countries, met in New Delhi, India, from 12 to 13 September 2026 for the XVIII BRICS Summit held under the theme: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.
2. We reaffirm our commitment to the BRICS spirit of mutual respect and understanding, sovereign equality, solidarity, democracy, openness, inclusiveness, collaboration and consensus. Building on two decades of BRICS, we further commit ourselves to strengthening cooperation in the expanded BRICS under the three pillars of political and security, economic and financial, cultural and people-to-people cooperation, and to enhancing our strategic partnership for the benefit of our people through the promotion of peace, a more representative, fairer international order, a reinvigorated and reformed multilateral system, sustainable development and inclusive growth.
3. We recognise the valuable contribution of Partner countries to BRICS cooperation. We underscore our strong belief that advancing the BRICS partnership with Emerging Markets and Developing Countries (EMDCs) will further contribute to strengthening the spirit of solidarity and international cooperation for the benefit of all. We reaffirm our commitment to fostering inclusive, mutually beneficial and development-oriented partnership with Partner countries. We encourage their increasing participation in BRICS engagements and practical cooperation in areas of shared interest.
4. We commend India for hosting the Outreach/BRICS Plus Dialogue segment of the 18th BRICS Summit, which injects new impetus to strengthen international cooperation and solidarity.
5. We commend the significant progress achieved under India’s BRICS Chairship in 2026, under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, which reflects our shared commitment to strengthening BRICS cooperation in addressing common challenges with a balanced, practical, actionable, inclusive, development-oriented and people-centered approach. We reaffirm our commitment to advancing cooperation on the thematic priorities, particularly through strengthening capacities, promoting innovation, and advancing sustainable development and resilience.
6.
